court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Civil Judge, Senior Division in Hindu Marriage Petition No.149 of 2003
case_name: Shri Yogesh Baburao Patil vs Sou. Rupali Yogesh Patil

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Yogesh Baburao Patil, husband, Real Estate Agent
parties.respondent_defendant: Sou. Rupali Yogesh Patil, wife, Household & Service

facts_of_case: Appellant and respondent were married in 2001. Respondent went to her parents' house for examination, then returned to matrimonial home. Out of wedlock, a male child was born in 2003. Appellant filed Hindu Marriage Petition No.149 of 2003 against respondent, praying for divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion.

legal_principles.principle: A court deciding a suit cannot decide only on the ground of cruelty and ignore other issues.
legal_principles.held: The learned trial judge was bound to decide the suit on the basis of all the issues involved in the suit and could not have decided only on the ground of cruelty.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 14 Rule 3

legal_principles.principle: A finding rendered by a court in one proceeding is not binding on another independent proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The said finding rendered in those proceedings would not be binding on the learned trial judge since the said proceedings filed by the appellant for seeking divorce was an independent proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: A court deciding a suit must render its finding or decision with reasons upon each separate issue.
legal_principles.held: The court shall render its finding or decision with the reasons upon each separate issue.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 20 Rule 5

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and decree dated 28th March, 2007 were upheld. The appeal was dismissed.
